LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD's top-level (global) scope, which is the only code executed by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, contains exclusively standard variable assignments and array definitions. Every global statement is either a literal string assignment (`_pkgver_sys='20.0-20260927'`, `_srcprefix=...`), a simple package metadata field (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`), or a `source_*` array whose elements are plain URL strings. There is no command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks), no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, and no obfuscation at global scope — nothing that downloads, executes, or transmits data while the PKGBUILD is sourced.

The only executable code present is the `package()` function, which references `system` and `vendor` images. This function is NOT invoked during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` (that command stops after sourcing the PKGBUILD), so it is out of scope for this gate and is audited separately. Note a packaging inconsistency (`.img` references vs `.zip` sources in `package()`) and a future-dated version number (`20260927`), but neither is malice and neither executes during this narrow command.

No network fetches, data exfiltration, or code execution occur at parse time. All declared sources point to SourceForge under the waydroid project, consistent with the package's own upstream URL.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Top-level only static variable assignments; no executable code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

The file appears benign and safe for inclusion in the AUR package.
